title: gate-axiom-law CLI options
description: The argv options accepted by `node scripts/gate-axiom-law.mjs` (parsed by parseArgv, scripts/gate-axiom-law.mjs:35-55). These are the only four flags read from argv; the census's packageRoot and leanSourcePath are NOT CLI options — they are fixed to DEFAULT_PACKAGE_ROOT and DEFAULT_LEAN_SOURCE_PATH inside main() and cannot be overridden from the command line (scripts/gate-axiom-law.mjs:22,25,140-141).

outDir.description: Corresponds to `--out-dir <path>` (scripts/gate-axiom-law.mjs:42-44). Passed through confinePath({root}) and defaults to DEFAULT_OUT_DIR, a fixed path under .../obsmetrological-services-section/data/records, when omitted (scripts/gate-axiom-law.mjs:26,138). Both the ratchet baseline file `<outDir>/axiom-law-baseline.json` (BASELINE_FILE_NAME, scripts/gate-axiom-law.mjs:27,142) and the dated gate record `<outDir>/<date>-axiom-law-gate.json` (scripts/gate-axiom-law.mjs:171) are written under this directory.

date.description: Corresponds to `--date <YYYY-MM-DD>` (scripts/gate-axiom-law.mjs:45-47). Defaults to todayStamp(), i.e. `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` in UTC, when omitted (scripts/gate-axiom-law.mjs:58-61,139). Used only to name the dated record file `<outDir>/<date>-axiom-law-gate.json` (scripts/gate-axiom-law.mjs:171); it does not affect the census or the gate decision.

init.description: Corresponds to the `--init` flag (scripts/gate-axiom-law.mjs:48-49, boolean, present/absent). Fed to decideBaselineUpdate (src/axiom-law-gate.mjs:130-139): when no baseline is on record it writes one at the current violation count (reason 'init'); it is a no-op once a baseline already exists (src/axiom-law-gate.mjs:131-134).

ratchet.description: Corresponds to the `--ratchet` flag (scripts/gate-axiom-law.mjs:50-51, boolean, present/absent). Fed to decideBaselineUpdate (src/axiom-law-gate.mjs:130-139): lowers an existing baseline to the current violation count only when it strictly improves on it (reason 'ratchet', src/axiom-law-gate.mjs:135-137); it never raises the baseline on a regression.
